name: echo-text

frames.best_why: A long fan of faded copies stretches out to the right, showing the echo effect at full stretch.

tagline: Ghost copies of a word trail behind it and lean with the cursor.
summary: A heavy white word with a train of faded, softly blurred copies behind it. The copies lag and stretch as the pointer moves, flare outward on a click, then gather back into one word.
appearance: One crisp white word dominates a pure black stage, with a row of paler duplicates stepping away behind it and dissolving into the dark. The copies grow steadily softer until only a faint smear of light remains.
behaviour: Moving the pointer toward a side pulls the copies that way while the front word leads, so the tail stretches and springs back. Clicking throws a few copies outward to fade, and the train vanishes when the pointer leaves.
use_when: A bold hero or section word where movement adds drama without changing the copy.
avoid_when: The copies smear into an unreadable fan on wide type, and the main effect needs a precise pointer.
customise: Set the word with text; echoes, lag, offset, direction, fade, blur, tint and outline style shape the trail. Mode, trail source, click burst, duration, easing and font size are props too.
weight_why: Up to twenty-four absolutely positioned text copies are moved each frame while the trail is awake.

a11y.note: Echo copies are hidden from assistive tech and removed under reduced motion; the trigger is pointer only.

issues: The copies are nearly the same white as the word, so the trail reads as plain blur rather than coloured ghosts.
polish_why: The trail moves cleanly, but identical white copies make it look like ordinary motion blur.
